Ever tried to set up disaster recovery for PostgreSQL on OCI and felt like you were juggling too many pieces?
That feeling changed with Oracle's latest update.
The new Full Stack DR now supports native PostgreSQL.
It means you can spin up a standby instance directly from the console without any extra layers.
Networking got a boost too.
Cross‑region VCN peering is now smoother and latency drops noticeably.
From a practical standpoint,
 here are three things I’m already testing:
- Full‑stack DR lets me provision a replica with a few clicks.
- Native PostgreSQL support removes the need for custom scripts or third‑party tools.
- The networking tweaks simplify VCN setup and improve failover speed.
I recommend running a scheduled failover drill now that the process is faster.
Also,
 enable automated backups and keep an eye on the new latency metrics.
These changes let us focus more on data quality and less on plumbing.
How are you planning to incorporate these new OCI features into your data pipeline?
#DataEngineering #PostgreSQL #OCI #DisasterRecovery

news_posts.post_content:
OpenAI announced today that its models will run on Google Cloud.

The deal means you can now access GPT‑4,
Claude‑like,
and other APIs from Google’s data centers.

It’s a clear expansion beyond the exclusive Microsoft Azure agreement that has been in place since 2020.

The fact is that Google will host the compute and storage for OpenAI’s inference workloads, according to CNBC.

My interpretation is that OpenAI is looking for redundancy and price competition, while Google gains AI‑ready services to attract developers.

For anyone building AI‑powered apps, this changes three things.

- You can choose the cloud provider that best fits your latency, cost, and compliance needs.
- Multi‑cloud strategies become easier because the same API endpoints are available on both Azure and Google Cloud.
- Data residency rules may be met by selecting the region that matches your regulatory requirements.

What impact will this have on your cloud roadmap?

concept_posts.post_content:
Ever stared at a dashboard and wondered why the trend line suddenly spikes and you have no idea if it's real or just noise?

In QuickSight, ML Insights and Forecasting let the service automatically detect anomalies and project future values without writing a single line of code.

Think of it like this: you have daily sales data for the past year.
You enable Forecast on the sales visual and QuickSight will suggest a 30‑day forward view,
 highlighting days that deviate from the expected pattern.

Here are a couple of things to keep in mind:

- The model works best with at least 30 data points; sparse data can produce unreliable forecasts.
- Review the confidence interval; a wide band means the model is uncertain,
 so treat those predictions cautiously.
- Enable anomaly detection on key metrics to catch outliers early and reduce manual monitoring.

A common mistake is trusting the forecast blindly without checking the underlying data quality or seasonality settings.

Have you tried using QuickSight’s forecasting on any of your own metrics?

#AWS #QuickSight #DataAnalytics #MachineLearning

Ever found yourself rebuilding the same training data for every model?
I used to spend hours pulling raw logs,
 cleaning them,
 and then re‑creating features for each experiment.
That’s why I started using a feature store.
A feature store is simply a centralized place where you define,
 compute,
 and serve features.
Think of it as a library of ready‑to‑use data columns that both data engineers and data scientists can access.
For example, we built a store for user activity features like daily active minutes,
 last purchase amount,
 and churn risk score.
Each feature is calculated once in our batch pipeline and then served in real time to models.

Key takeaways:
- Consistency between training and serving data reduces drift.
- Re‑using features cuts engineering time by up to 40%.
- Versioning lets you roll back to a known good set of features.

Common mistake to avoid: treating the feature store as just another data lake.
If you don’t enforce schema and monitoring, you’ll end up with stale or mismatched features.

How do you currently manage feature reuse in your projects?

#DataEngineering #FeatureStore #MachineLearning #AI
